messages:
joan: FYI I deployed Kelp-v3-int5 (per-channel quant, no stoch) to staging for embeddings. doing a quick QA sweep today.
sam: cool. I'll run recall@1,5,10 on short/medium/long buckets + topk_entropy. baseline = tide-emb-v1.
lee: include multilingual slice and filter isolated-punctuation queries from short bucket. freeze tokenizer v1.4 for parity.
eval-bot: Job 222900 queued by sam. model=kelp-v3-int5 dataset=prod-simset-25k seeds=3 microbatches=64.
sam: early numbers: global recall@1 -0.9% abs vs baseline; short recall@1 -3.4% abs; recall@10 short -0.8%. medium/long within +/-0.5%.
lee: ouch on short. can you paste 8 failing short queries with top5? need to know swap vs drift.
sam: sample dump:
```
q: "reset password"
baseline top1: "how to reset password" (cos=0.88)
kelp top1: "account recovery steps" (cos=0.83)
kelp top2: "how to reset password" (cos=0.81)
```
seems like top1 swaps / tight margins.
joan: likely tie flips from precision reduction. try post-quant per-channel bias correction.
sam: re-ran with bias-corr: short recall@1 gap 3.4% -> 1.1%. recall@5 nearly matched baseline.
lee: nice. what about perf/cost?
joan: cost down ~17% per token; latency p50 similar with kv-cache off.
sam: action items: 1) run 100k holdout with bias-corr and selective-fp16 for projection layers; 2) lee prepare 25 qualitative failing examples for model card; 3) ops add canary fallback to tide-emb-v1 if short_recall1_drop >2% or topk_entropy delta >0.1.
ops-bot: Canary rule queued: fallback=tide-emb-v1 trigger_short_recall1_drop_pct=2.0 topk_entropy_delta=0.1 window_mins=5.
eval-bot: Holdout job 222901 started (100k, metrics=recall@1,5,10;silhouette;topk_entropy;centroid_shift). ETA ~50m.
sam: also generating uMAP delta and cosine-centroid shift for short cluster, will attach to ticket.
lee: note: tokenization edgecases (emoji-only) add noise; we should exclude them from SLOs.
joan: agreed. if holdout meets thresholds (recall@1 gap <=1.5% and cost reduction >=15%) we can proceed to canary with fallback + 24h norm/entropy monitor. thanks all.
